title: Prefetching Strategies
description: Learn advanced prefetching strategies to make your React Query application feel instant.

data.text: Welcome to this comprehensive guide on **Prefetching Strategies**. Learn advanced prefetching strategies to make your React Query application feel instant. In today's rapidly evolving technology landscape, understanding this topic is crucial for any developer looking to build robust, scalable, and maintainable applications. This lesson will take you from fundamental concepts to advanced implementations, providing you with practical knowledge you can apply immediately. Whether you are a beginner taking your first steps or an experienced developer looking to deepen your expertise, this guide has something valuable for you. We will explore theoretical foundations, practical implementations, real-world scenarios, and common pitfalls to avoid. By the end of this lesson, you will have a thorough understanding of Prefetching Strategies and be confident in applying it to your projects.
Why Prefetch?

Users perceive a site as fast when transitions feel instant. Even if your API is blazing fast, the round-trip time between navigation and data availability creates a perceptible delay. Prefetching narrows this gap by loading data in anticipation of user intent.

data.title: The Perception Gap
data.text: A 200ms network delay feels acceptable on load, but noticeable during navigation. Prefetching bridges this gap by loading data while the user is still on the previous page.
prefetchQuery vs fetchQuery

React Query offers two programmatic methods for fetching data outside of a component. `prefetchQuery` loads data and populates the cache without subscribing to updates, while `fetchQuery` returns a Promise that resolves with the data. Both are useful, but they serve slightly different purposes.

data.title: Basic prefetchQuery
data.content: Prefetching data for a user profile

data.text: Hover Prefetching

Hover prefetching is one of the most effective patterns for improving perceived performance. When a user hovers over a link or button, you have a strong signal that they intend to navigate. You can use this idle time to fetch data before they click.

data.title: Hover Prefetch with Links
Debounce Hover Prefetching
data.text: Avoid prefetching on every mouseEnter event. Use a short debounce (50-100ms) to ensure the user is actually hovering intentionally, not just passing the cursor across the screen.
Route Change Prefetching

Many modern routers support route prefetching out of the box. By prefetching the entire page or specific queries on route change, you ensure that when the user lands on a new page, the data is already in the cache.

data.caption: Prefetch data flow from hover to navigation
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant L as Link
    participant Q as QueryClient
    participant A as API

    U->>L: Hovers over link
    L->>Q: prefetchQuery(queryKey, queryFn)
    Q->>A: Fetch data
    A-->>Q: Return data
    Q->>Q: Store in cache
    U->>L: Clicks link
    L->>Q: useQuery(queryKey)
    Q-->>L: Return cached data instantly

data.text: Prefetching Multiple Queries

Some pages require multiple queries. You can prefetch them all in parallel to reduce total wait time. Use `Promise.all` with multiple `prefetchQuery` calls to ensure the cache is fully populated before the user navigates.

data.title: Prefetching Multiple Queries
data.content: Prefetching a dashboard's data in parallel

data.title: Avoid Over-Prefetching
data.text: Prefetching every link on a page can saturate the user's network and waste bandwidth. Focus on high-intent elements like primary navigation, product cards, and pagination links.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: prefetchQuery loads data into cache without subscribing
fetchQuery returns a Promise with the data
Debounce hover events to avoid wasting requests
Balance prefetching against bandwidth and cost
data.takeaway: Prefetching transforms reactive loading into proactive loading, making apps feel instant.

data.text: Common Mistakes to Avoid

Even experienced developers can fall into these traps when working with **Prefetching Strategies**. Being aware of these common mistakes will help you write better code and avoid costly debugging sessions:

items: **Over-Engineering**: Using advanced features of Prefetching Strategies when a simple solution suffices. Always start with the simplest approach that meets your requirements and add complexity only when justified.
**Ignoring Edge Cases**: Failing to handle null values, empty states, and boundary conditions leads to runtime errors and poor user experience.
**Copy-Paste Without Understanding**: Using code snippets without fully understanding their implications creates hidden bugs and security vulnerabilities.
**Neglecting Testing**: Assuming code works without tests is a recipe for production incidents. Write tests that verify behavior and prevent regressions.
**Performance Blindness**: Ignoring performance implications until they become critical issues. Profile early and optimize based on data, not assumptions.
**Hardcoding Configuration**: Embedding values directly in code instead of using environment variables and configuration files.
**Tight Coupling**: Creating dependencies that make code difficult to test, modify, or reuse. Favor composition over inheritance.
**Inconsistent Error Handling**: Mixing different error handling patterns makes code unpredictable and hard to debug.

data.text: Performance Considerations

Performance is a critical aspect of any production application. When implementing **Prefetching Strategies**, consider these optimization strategies to ensure your application remains fast and responsive:

items: **Lazy Loading**: Defer non-critical operations until they are actually needed to reduce initial load time.
**Caching**: Implement intelligent caching strategies to avoid redundant computations and network requests.
**Memoization**: Cache results of expensive function calls to improve performance for repeated operations.
**Batch Processing**: Group multiple operations together to reduce overhead and improve throughput.
**Resource Management**: Properly clean up resources, event listeners, and subscriptions to prevent memory leaks.
**Profiling**: Use performance profiling tools to identify bottlenecks before optimizing.
**Bundle Size**: Minimize dependencies and use tree-shaking to reduce application bundle size.
**Network Optimization**: Reduce payload sizes, use compression, and implement efficient data fetching strategies.

data.text: Security Considerations
Security should never be an afterthought. When implementing **Prefetching Strategies**, keep these security best practices in mind to protect your application and users:

items: **Input Validation**: Always validate and sanitize user input to prevent injection attacks.
**Authentication and Authorization**: Implement proper access controls and verify user permissions.
**Secrets Management**: Never hardcode API keys, passwords, or tokens. Use environment variables and secret management services.
**HTTPS**: Always use HTTPS in production to encrypt data in transit.
**Content Security Policy**: Implement CSP headers to mitigate XSS attacks.
**Dependency Scanning**: Regularly scan dependencies for known vulnerabilities.
**Rate Limiting**: Protect APIs from abuse with appropriate rate limiting.
**Audit Logging**: Log security-relevant events for monitoring and incident response.
